interpretation: Review IDs are distinct from repository requirement IDs. Source-confirmed does not mean runtime reproduced. P1/P2 are development priorities, not CVSS.

findings.title: Host-side AGENTS.md reads can disclose files outside the jail
findings.preconditions: A workspace instruction symlink targets a readable host text file; a following prompt is constructed.
findings.impact: External bytes can enter a local or remote model request without a read_file approval or jail access.
acceptance: A dummy external sentinel never appears in a captured fake-provider system prompt.
Regular instruction refresh and explicitly permitted internal links still work.
Cover replacement during read, broken/looped links and adjacent skill metadata ingress.
findings.repair: Confinement-aware host metadata reads with a defined symlink/secure-open policy.

findings.title: Approved file aliases can mutate protected/shared targets
findings.preconditions: A reachable alias points into protected Git metadata or the live dependency tree; the ordinary approval policy permits the file action, including per-chat auto-approval.
findings.impact: Host file writes bypass protected-target refusal and jail mount permissions. The ordinary approval policy still applies; auto-approved tools need no fresh human prompt.
acceptance: Alias write/edit and directory-alias child deletion leave protected sentinels unchanged.
Readable shared dependencies remain readable but are not writable by host file tools.
Final-symlink deletion and concurrent target replacement follow the specified policy.
findings.repair: Separate read reachability from canonical writable-target policy and synchronize the decisive mutation check.

findings.title: Overlay mount lock remains held throughout the command
findings.preconditions: Two commands need the same worktree dependency overlay while the first command remains running.
findings.impact: Ready commands unnecessarily serialize and consume other commands' deadline budget.
acceptance: A ready-but-held command A does not prevent command B from completing.
Mount setup remains serialized and retries reacquire correctly.
Queue timeout, holder death and terminal starts release ownership correctly.
findings.repair: Release at readiness, retain failure cleanup, and bound acquisition by the remaining command deadline.

findings.title: Folder-tool jail mounts the skill directory instead of the workspace
findings.preconditions: A real jailed folder script needs project files outside its own skill folder.
findings.impact: ELIA_WORKSPACE names a project whose source and Git metadata may be absent from the jail.
acceptance: A jailed script retains skill cwd and reads a project sentinel through ELIA_WORKSPACE.
An outside sibling sentinel remains inaccessible.
Cover external project, Elia worktree and global skill cases.
findings.repair: Separate confinement root from cwd and supply narrow extra skill-directory mounts.

findings.title: External-project children receive Elia's global workspace
findings.preconditions: spawn_task runs from a non-harness project whose folder differs from Elia's root.
findings.impact: File/shell effects, Git baseline, lock and result reporting can target the wrong repository despite correct project labels.
acceptance: Child pwd/read/write and Git result all refer to the external parent workspace.
Elia fixture tree is unchanged.
Distinct external projects do not share a false writer lock; resume uses the correct baseline.
findings.repair: Resolve one authoritative actual parent workspace for every project and retain only the Elia worktree special case.

findings.title: A dead session can leave its unlinked loop and tools running
findings.preconditions: A session terminates/crashes while the application and its independent task supervisor remain up.
findings.impact: Orphan work can continue and overlap a reopened/resumed session for the same chat.
acceptance: Terminating only the session kills its held loop/worker without test-side cleanup.
Abrupt kill is covered by ownership monitoring, not terminate/2 alone.
Reopen has only one active turn; ordinary Stop and approval cleanup still work.
findings.repair: Bind loop lifetime to session ownership while preserving one-way tool-crash isolation.

findings.title: Decodable malformed chat shapes crash shared load/list paths
findings.preconditions: A valid encoded term contains invalid chat fields, such as messages:nil.
findings.impact: One invalid record can disrupt listing and the boot resume scan, beyond opening that one chat.
acceptance: Malformed roots, messages, blocks, times and task metadata are isolated.
Other valid chats still list and resume.
Supported legacy shapes and raw provider data remain intact.
findings.repair: Validate/normalize at the stored-record boundary and preserve diagnostic/quarantine information.

findings.title: A failed save clears the only dirty/shutdown-retry signal
findings.preconditions: A final save fails, storage recovers, and a session closes without a later mutation.
findings.impact: Completion remains unsaved; an older active-turn marker can cause later replay of already-completed work.
acceptance: Injected final-write failure retains dirty state until successful recovery.
Graceful shutdown retries recovered storage without a later message.
Permanent failures remain bounded and do not corrupt previous saved bytes.
findings.repair: Track dirty generation independently of timer presence and clear it only after durable success.

findings.title: Terminal transport does not enforce browser origin/session proof
findings.preconditions: An unrelated origin knows an existing terminal chat ID and browser/proxy policy permits reaching the endpoint.
findings.impact: That origin can read terminal output and send input subject to the terminal's actual jail.
acceptance: Transport handshake rejects foreign origin and missing/invalid session proof.
Same-origin and configured reverse-proxy clients still connect.
Byte encoding, overflow/rejoin and confinement behavior remain correct.
findings.repair: Add explicit origin allowlisting and validated session/CSRF or purpose-scoped token checks.

findings.title: Terminal Start and its warning use stale or prospective jail state
findings.preconditions: Jail changes in another tab after a terminal page mounts, or an existing terminal outlives a preference change.
findings.impact: A newly started terminal can run unjailed after the preference is enabled; labels can hide an already unjailed process.
acceptance: Two-view setting change is reflected at Start.
Existing-terminal warning follows actual status.jail.
Define prospective preference separately from existing process lifetime.
findings.repair: Fetch authoritative settings at Start and show actual process confinement while it exists.

findings.title: Push initialization and subscription changes lose concurrent updates
findings.preconditions: Concurrent first key requests, subscriptions, or registration racing with endpoint cleanup.
findings.impact: Different VAPID keys can be returned or device updates lost, preventing later notifications.
acceptance: Simultaneous initialization returns the same persisted pair.
Concurrent independent subscriptions both survive.
Removal/clear ordering cannot be undone by stale writers.
findings.repair: Serialize complete get-or-create and read/modify/write transactions, not individual calls.

findings.title: Unavailable project root crashes the Files page fallback
findings.preconditions: A registered external folder is moved, removed, unreadable or unmounted.
findings.impact: A failed fallback assigns an error atom as entries; rendering raises instead of presenting a usable error state.
acceptance: Visiting a vanished project root displays an error and keeps the picker usable.
entries always remains a list.
No silent switch into another project's files.
findings.repair: Pattern-match the fallback result and render a safe empty listing with the real root error.

findings.title: Documented clean setup omits required Node package installation
findings.preconditions: Fresh checkout without assets/node_modules follows the README mix setup sequence.
findings.impact: Asset builds lack xterm dependencies; Node's documented optional status is misleading.
acceptance: Literal README setup succeeds from a clean checkout.
Required CSS/JS bundles and terminal hook work.
A repeat setup is safe and dependency install is reproducible.
findings.repair: Install locked Node dependencies in the setup path and correct prerequisites.

findings.title: Rejected deploy can leave served generated bundles damaged
findings.preconditions: Candidate asset generation changes/removes output then fails; generated assets are ignored as in the real checkout.
findings.impact: Git resets while old server code can serve new, partial or missing asset bytes. Watchers provide no transactional guarantee.
acceptance: Failed build restores revision-A HTTP asset bytes as well as Git state.
Use ignored generated assets in the fixture, unlike the current committed-bundle fixture.
Cover partial write, deletion, truncation, failed rollback and no-merge deployment.
findings.repair: Stage and atomically promote/restore verified asset bundles with coordinated watchers.

findings.title: Restart availability does not check for an external supervisor
findings.preconditions: Deployment-ready tree is launched directly with mix phx.server and no restarting supervisor.
findings.impact: Restart is accepted, then the server stops without a replacement.
acceptance: Bare launch disables/rejects Restart with a useful prerequisite message.
Supervised launch replaces the process.
Hot reload capability remains independent.
findings.repair: Separate restart-supervisor readiness from Mix/code-reloader availability.

findings.title: Slow manual/turn-start summaries block the session and callers
findings.preconditions: Eligible nonempty aged-out history requires a summary taking longer than the default five-second call timeout.
findings.impact: LiveView can time out while the session remains blocked; Stop/snapshot queue and a turn can start later.
acceptance: Held summarizer does not kill the initiating LiveView or block control calls.
Stop cancels pending preparation; late results cannot start a turn.
Cover manual and turn-start paths; retain summary-failure fallback.
findings.repair: Run monitored compaction work outside the session callback with explicit generation/operation ownership.

findings.title: Nonnumeric SSE error codes raise during error handling
findings.preconditions: An HTTP-200 error chunk has a symbolic/invalid string code; current providers emitting it was not established.
findings.impact: The parser loses a useful provider message to an exception instead of returning the error contract.
acceptance: Numeric integers/strings classify correctly.
Unknown, absent, null and unexpected code types return useful errors without raising.
Unknown codes do not automatically become transient.
findings.repair: Pattern-match Integer.parse and explicitly handle nonnumeric/partial values.
